gloss: dressed meat; butchered meat for sale

definitions.gloss: dressed meat; butchered meat ready for sale
definitions.explanation: Meat that has been processed and prepared for retail sale, as distinct from a live animal or whole carcass. Commonly seen as a department label in supermarkets.

examples.japanese: {精肉|せいにく}コーナーで{豚肉|ぶたにく}を{買|か}った。
examples.english: I bought pork at the meat counter.

examples.japanese: あの{精肉|せいにく}{店|てん}は{質|しつ}のいい{牛肉|ぎゅうにく}で{有名|ゆうめい}だ。
examples.english: That butcher shop is famous for high-quality beef.

examples.japanese: スーパーの{精肉|せいにく}{売|う}り{場|ば}では、{国産|こくさん}と{輸入|ゆにゅう}の{肉|にく}が{分|わ}けて{並|なら}べられている。
examples.english: At the supermarket meat section, domestic and imported meats are displayed separately.

notes:
A compound of {精|せい} (refined, processed) and {肉|にく} (meat). Refers to meat that has been butchered and prepared for cooking.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {精肉|せいにく}{店|てん} (butcher shop)
- {精肉|せいにく}コーナー (meat section in a supermarket)
- {精肉|せいにく}{売|う}り{場|ば} (meat sales area)

In Japanese supermarkets, the main fresh food departments are typically labeled {青果|せいか} (produce), {精肉|せいにく} (meat), {鮮魚|せんぎょ} (fresh fish), and {惣菜|そうざい} (prepared foods/deli).
